decisions.reason: The address autocomplete service builds on the firm's established data and web service infrastructure, costs little to run, and fits the announced SaaS platform direction, so management sees no reason to abandon it.

The Austrian gas grid fee database extends the firm's core database expertise to a new country and reflects a visible expansion commitment that management would justify by pointing to a slow, temporary ramp-up in a new market.
Peak load window determination is a regulated calculation service close to the firm's core analytical offer for network operators, so it stays as part of the integrated process portfolio.
The end-customer tariff database is a multi-model product line in which the firm has invested heavily, and it is central to the firm's market data business and platform strategy.
Custom web services embody the announced move toward broader end-to-end digital service provision and reuse existing infrastructure, so they are retained.
The postal code lookup service is a low-cost complement to the address and tariff data services, built on long-maintained databases, and it supports the modular SaaS offering.
